constraint_review: Span 40 m; first vertical mode about 1.9 Hz: Met. The design retains the existing 40 m span and places the cross-beam at the midspan antinode, with bare frequency 1.9 Hz, optimum tune 1.83 Hz and locked-mass check 1.86 Hz.
feedback:
This twin under-deck tuned mass damper retrofit works physically and should go to detail design. Bridge motion at the midspan antinode drives two sprung masses out of phase and paired viscous dampers turn relative motion into heat, the clamped cross-beam carries the forces into the girders by friction, and a midspan accelerometer logger files the comfort verdict, so load path, energy path and signal path are all continuous. My biggest worry is not the principle but the two placeholders every concept must carry at this stage, namely the assumed 20 tonne modal mass that sizes everything and the assumed available depth between girders that must swallow the hanging hardware, and both look plausible enough to release with survey confirmation in detail design. The approach compares directly with the closest prior art, a 44.6 m steel box footbridge retrofitted with two 500 kgf vertical units at the central section and DEICON-type 500 kg combined under-deck units at midspan concealed in the structure with locked versus unlocked accelerometer proof, and this concept keeps that proven twin hidden midspan architecture while adding a deliberate detuned pair, a weld-free clamped beam with stops, and a quantified Medium-band filing that prior work did not disclose.

I checked every deciding number by re-deriving the physical relation and recomputing. Modal stiffness follows k equals M times 2 pi f squared for a single mode in the linear regime, which for 20000 kg at 1.9 Hz gives 142.5 times 20000 equals 2.85e6 N per m as shown in the stiffness calc (E12). Mass ratio mu equals damper mass divided by modal mass, so 0.04 times 20000 equals 800 kg total or 400 kg per unit (E13) with the per-unit split (E52). Den Hartog tuning for an undamped primary in the fixed-points regime gives optimum damper frequency f2 equals f1 divided by 1 plus mu, so 1.9 divided by 1.04 equals 1.83 Hz (E14), and optimum damper ratio zeta equals square root of 3 mu divided by 8 times 1 plus mu, so square root of 0.01442 equals 12.0 percent (E15). Damper stiffness follows k2 equals m times 2 pi f2 squared, so 800 kg at 1.827 Hz gives about 1.05e5 N per m (E16), and damper coefficient follows c equals 2 zeta times square root of k times m, giving about 2.21e3 N s per m, consistent with the free-decay simulation that reports 6.2 percent effective damping with 49.4 mm peak relative travel from a 20 mm release (E17). Static sag follows delta equals m g divided by k, so 7848 N divided by 105000 N per m equals 0.0747 m or 74.7 mm (E63), and sag plus stroke gives 74.7 plus 49.4 equals 124 mm envelope (E68). Slip resistance per high-strength friction-grip bolt follows mu-slip times preload divided by gamma, so 0.3 times 137000 N divided by 1.25 equals 32.9 kN per bolt (E64), against combined static plus dynamic demand of 7848 N plus 5220 N equals 13.1 kN total (E65), where the dynamic part follows F equals m times omega squared times X, so 800 times 11.5 squared times 0.0494 equals 5.22e3 N (E29). Stop force follows k times compression, so 105000 times 0.08 equals 8.4 kN (E66). Locked frequency with damper seized follows f times square root of M divided by M plus m for added mass on the same stiffness, so 1.9 times square root of 20 over 20.8 equals 1.86 Hz (E69). Crowd load follows density times area, so 0.5 per m2 times 120 m2 for a 40 m by 3 m deck gives 60 pedestrians (E40) with total live load of 5 kN per m2 times 120 m2 equals 600 kN (E30). Equivalent synchronized pedestrians 5.92 from the 10.8 times square root of zeta times N rule (E41) times 280 N per person gives about 1660 N modal force, or 0.0828 N per kg when divided by 20000 kg (E42). Resonant acceleration for harmonic excitation at resonance in steady state follows force over mass divided by 2 zeta, so 0.0828 divided by 0.01 equals 8.28 m per s2 bare (E43) and 0.0828 divided by 0.124 equals 0.67 m per s2 with 6.2 percent effective damping (E44), as confirmed by the time simulation reaching 0.67 m per s2 retrofitted versus 4.9 to 6.9 m per s2 bare at 15 to 30 s with Maximum below 0.5, Medium 0.5 to 1.0, Minimum 1.0 to 2.5 and unacceptable above 2.5 m per s2 (E45), and holding 0.476 to 0.526 m per s2 under detuning (E70).

The design agrees with itself. Parts list names one 2.5 to 3.0 m cross-beam, two 400 kg masses, two coil springs, two viscous dampers, four M20 bolts, two caged stops, one logger and two existing girders, and connections hang masses from the beam on springs in parallel with dampers to the beam, clamp the beam to the girders by friction, cage the stops to the beam under the masses, and mount the logger at midspan, matching the operating sequence of beam moves, masses swing, dampers heat, clamps carry, stops catch and logger files. Constraint table places units at midspan of the 40 m span (E55) with off-antinode penalty 0.75 (E67), tunes 1.83 Hz from 1.9 Hz with 1.86 Hz locked (E14)(E69), and keeps all steel within girder depth with nothing above deck (E55). The failed xkcd sketch followed by a readable layout sketch of deck, girders, midspan beam, hung masses, clamps, stops and access side (E55) settles placement.

For worst case of every limit, the hardest resonant crowd at 1.9 Hz Class III is already used for the 8.28 to 0.67 m per s2 claim, the hardest mechanical load of static weight plus full dynamic stroke at 13.1 kN total is well below four times 32.9 kN slip capacity even if both stops hit at 8.4 kN each, the 49.4 mm stroke is inside the 80 mm stop gap measured from static equilibrium with 124 mm sag-plus-stroke kept between girders, and the 1.86 Hz locked shift proves damping rather than frequency shift must do the work so detuning to plus or minus 5 percent was swept and still stays Medium. Holding over time is by four bolts with lock-nuts plus annual below-bridge-vehicle re-torque and annual re-tune with lock pins for service, which is reasonable at concept for preload loss at 1.9 Hz and tuning drift.

On the four must-not-skip checks: (0) every function has a means, with capture by the clamped cross-beam at the antinode, counterforce by the twin 400 kg pair detuned about 1.83 Hz, dissipation by the paired dampers in a tolerant band, transfer by the friction-clamped beam into the girders as shear, travel limit by caged stops with pads and pins, appearance by all hardware between girders below soffit, and verification by the crowd walk-through logger versus bands, and the chief designer left no function without a means. (1) For size and mass limits I summed what the board names: added weight 7.85 kN (E26) over 600 kN live load (E30) equals 1.31 percent (E72) against the 2 percent rule, vertical stack of mass height 400 to 600 mm plus spring length 200 to 400 mm plus 124 mm sag-plus-stroke envelope must sit in girder depth that the board shows only by sketch annotation (E55) without a girder-depth dimension, and cross-beam length 2.5 to 3.0 m must span between girders and carry two side-by-side masses of about 370 mm cubes, which fits a 3 m wide deck on everyday scale but needs a surveyed clearance sketch in detail design. (1b) Every numeric given constraint is computed from the design's own values, with span by layout at midspan and frequency by 1.9 Hz bare with 1.83 Hz tune and 1.86 Hz locked, not by words alone. (2) The board gives two values for added-weight fraction, 0.133 percent from dividing 800 kg by 600000 N mixing mass and force (E71) and 1.31 percent from 7.85 over 600 in consistent force units (E72); the design correctly uses 1.31 percent and both meet the 2 percent rule so the error does not affect acceptance but the wrong-unit calc should be struck. (3) Energy flows from vertical bridge vibration into the cross-beam, into out-of-phase motion of the tuned blocks on coil springs, into heat in the viscous units back to the beam and by friction into the girders with over-travel bridged by the caged stops, and signal flows from the bolted midspan accelerometer through conditioner into the crowd-run logger into the filed band verdict, with consecutive parts meeting at midspan below soffit in the same under-deck bay and no gap or double placement. (4) There are no open objections and all members recorded ready on dynamics, weight versus stiffening, clamp and stops, and Medium proof, so the meeting facts leave the concept settled.

Scales and sources support release. Bare 8.28 m per s2 is about 0.84 g, violent and clearly unacceptable, while 0.67 m per s2 is about 0.07 g, noticeable but in the Medium strolling range, and 400 kg is about five adults, 7.85 kN about 800 kgf, and 49 mm stroke plus 75 mm sag about a hand width, all ordinary shop sizes. Key claims that rest on no opened source must be noticed: modal mass 20000 kg has only calculation with no deck-mass survey or mode-shape integration, girder depth and below-soffit clearance have only the layout sketch with no dimensioned stack, spring rate 105 kN per m and damper units have no catalogue datasheet search, and comfort bands 0.5, 1.0 and 2.5 m per s2 rest on search results never opened (E33)(E34) plus weaker comfort searches (E19) and a failed vetted Den Hartog call (E10) already covered by hand calcs. Stiffening to 2.3 Hz needing 46.5 percent more stiffness (E27) and to 2.5 Hz needing 73.1 percent (E28) rightly rules out stiffening, and robustness from multiple detuned units (E48), midspan most-effective-location precedent (E46)(E47) and maintenance access guidance (E49) are read from opened pages. None of the gaps breaks the working principle or buildability with purchasable steel, springs, fluid dampers, M20 bolts and loggers by bolting without weld or deck opening, so they belong as detail-design confirmations of surveyed modal mass and frequency, ordered spring and damper datasheets with re-tune range, dimensioned clearance versus girder depth, and filed Class III walk-through records, not as blocks to this concept.
